summary: Leedom Lefferts worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2011, he served as Professor Emeritus of Anthropology at Drew University and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Michigan by 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College.

Leo Frobenius was an archaeologist and historian. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), the Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte.

Leo M. Pruden was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Taitetsu Unno and Akira Hirakawa, attending the University of Tokyo (1964–1966). He taught at Brown University, the Nyingma Institute, and the University of Oriental Studies.

Linguist Leo Meyer studied at the University of Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin under Theodor Benfey, Jacob Grimm, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Göttingen and served as professor at the University of Tartu (1865–1899).
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indology scholar. As attested in 2026, he studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter.

Philosopher Leo Strauss studied at Marburg, Hamburg, Freiburg, and Columbia. His main academic posts included appointments at the University of Cambridge (~1934–1937), The New School (~1938–1949), and the University of Chicago (~1949–1969).

Leon Hurvitz was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He held professorships at the University of Washington from circa 1955 to 1971 and at the University of British Columbia from circa 1971 to 1988.

Linguist Leonard Bloomfield studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Cincinnati, Illinois, and Ohio State, before serving as Sterling Professor of Linguistics at Yale University from 1940 to 1949.
Leonard Blussé is a historian and sinologist. He studied at Leiden University circa 1965 to 1970 and subsequently held an academic post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teacher F. E. L. Priestley, holding a post at the University of Toronto attested in 1991.

Leonard Swidler studied at St. Norbert College, Marquette, Wisconsin, Tübingen, and Munich. A scholar of religious studies and philosophy, he taught at Duquesne University before serving as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).
Leonard Woolley was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He received his education at St John's School, Leatherhead, from circa 1893 to 1899 and at New College from circa 1899 to 1903.
Leonard Zwilling was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1976.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He taught at the University of Washington and became Sanskrit department chair at Harvard in 1995.
Leonid Kulikov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He held an attested post at Leiden University in 2007 and serves on the faculty at Ghent University, attested in 2026.

Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette, Oregon, and Yale. He served as a professor at Yale University beginning in 1956 and as an anthropology curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History from circa 1956 to 1993.

Indologist Leopold von Schroeder studied at Tartu under Leo Meyer, and at Jena and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu, the University of Innsbruck (1896), and the University of Vienna (1899).

Leslie S. Kawamura specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther in 1975 and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary (~1976–2011).

Levi McLaughlin works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University. He held positions at Kokugakuin University, Wofford College, NUS, Iowa, and North Carolina State University.
